summary: Dose 1 to 3 are in the stage-1 (low-defect) regime. The D/G height ratio rises 0.25 → 0.57 → 1.19, which maps to inter-defect distance L_D ≈ 24 → 16 → 11 nm and defect density ≈ 5.5e10 → 1.3e11 → 2.6e11 cm⁻² (about ×5, ±~35% from the calibration constant). Dose 4 is past the D/G maximum (stage 2, amorphisation): D/G has fallen to 0.58 while the G band broadened ×3.3 and up-shifted by +11 cm⁻¹, and the 2D band has nearly vanished. The lower D/G at dose 4 means lost sp² crystallinity, not fewer defects, so no L_D or defect density can be read from it with the stage-1 relation. Dose 4 is the most damaged spectrum. Absolute defect density per step is therefore only defined for doses 1 to 3.

observations.finding: D/G height ratio (Lorentzian fits, 532 nm): dose1 0.250, dose2 0.569, dose3 1.191, dose4 0.584; area ratios 0.26, 0.60, 1.26, 0.76. Dose 1 to 3 are stable to <1% across fit windows (1150-1800 and 1200-1750 cm-1) and baseline order (linear or quadratic); dose 4 spans 0.57-0.63.
observations.evidence: Single-spectrum Lorentzian fits of D (1346-1352 cm-1), G (1580-1592 cm-1) and D' (1611-1622 cm-1) on a local polynomial baseline, scipy curve_fit, per-spectrum fit. Despiked one cosmic ray in dose2 at 2154.08 cm-1 (7466 counts vs ~300 neighbours) before fitting; Si line is outside D/G window.

observations.finding: Dose 1 to 3 lie on the stage-1 branch: the D/G ratio increases with dose and G FWHM stays at ~14 cm-1 (13.8-14.0). Using L_D^2 = 1.8e-9 * lambda^4 / (I_D/I_G) with lambda = 532 nm gives L_D = 24.0 nm (20-27), 15.9 nm (13.5-18), 11.0 nm (9.4-12.4). Defect density with n_D = 1e14/(pi L_D^2) gives 5.5e10, 1.3e11, 2.6e11 cm^-2 (ranges 4.3-7.6e10, 9.8e10-1.7e11, 2.1-3.6e11). Using area ratios instead of heights changes L_D by <3%.
observations.evidence: lambda^4 = 8.01e10 nm^4, C*lambda^4 = 144.2 nm^2. Range from C = (1.8 +/- 0.5)e-9 nm^2. Dose 3 at L_D ≈ 11 nm sits at the lower edge of the stated validity (L_D >= 10 nm).
observations.source: arXiv:1105.0175 (Cancado et al., Nano Lett. 2011 as I recall it; in the iopic-bond library): Fig. 4 and its text (low-defect regime L_D >= 10 nm; solid curve E_L^4 (I_D/I_G) vs L_D). My reading of the Fig. 4 solid curve is E_L^4 (I_D/I_G) ≈ 4250/L_D^2 eV^4 nm^2, consistent with C ≈ 1.8e-9 nm^2 within the paper's stated ±30%. I did not parse the equation text directly.

observations.finding: Dose 4 is past the D/G maximum (stage 2). G FWHM jumps from 13.8-14.0 to 44.7-49.1 cm-1, G moves from 1580.4 to 1591.5 cm-1 (+11), and the 2D/G height ratio falls from ~3.0 to ~0.06.
observations.evidence: Dose 1 to 3: 2D height/G height 3.02, 2.98, 2.97; 2D FWHM 31.9-32.1 cm-1. Dose 4: 2D fit runs into its width bound (FWHM 120 cm-1, height 186), so the 2D value is not reliable, though the collapse is large (~50x) and robust. D' is merged into G at dose 4 (fitted I_D'/I_G = 0.05 with ±20 cm-1 uncertainty), so the G position is a merged G+D' value.

observations.finding: The G-width behaviour is what separates stage 1 from stage 2 here. Before the D/G maximum G FWHM is constant ~14 cm-1 and the G dispersion is zero; the broadening onset coincides with the D/G maximum.
observations.evidence: Dose 1 to 3 at constant G FWHM 13.8-14.0 cm-1; dose 4 at 45-49 cm-1, i.e. ×3.3.
observations.source: arXiv:1105.0175, Fig. 5(c) caption and text: G FWHM 'remains roughly constant at ~14 cm-1 until the onset of the second stage of amorphization, corresponding to the maximum I_D/I_G'; Fig. 3: I_D/I_G increases as L_D decreases (stage 1), peaks at L_D ~3 nm, falls to zero below 3 nm (stage 2).

observations.finding: The Si 520.9 cm-1 line is the same in all four spectra (scatter < 0.1 cm-1), so the spectrometer calibration is stable and the G shift at dose 4 is not a calibration artifact. Si intensity varies 4646-6846 counts (±20%) between steps, so focus or alignment changed between acquisitions.
Dose 1 to 3 look like a monolayer from the 2D band alone: 2D FWHM ~32 cm-1 and 2D/G ≈ 3.0. I did not verify a literature source for these thresholds in this session.
observations.evidence: Single-spectrum fits; dose 1 2D FWHM 32.1, dose 2 31.9, dose 3 32.0; 2D/G height 3.0 in each.

observations.finding: I_D'/I_G rises with the D band in stage 1 (0.04, 0.09, 0.17 for dose 1-3) and drops at dose 4 (0.05, merged with G).
observations.evidence: D' heights from the three-Lorentzian fit; the dose 4 D' fit is poorly constrained (FWHM ±22 cm-1).

caveats: Stage 1 vs stage 2 for dose 3 rests on G FWHM staying ~14 cm-1 (13.8-13.9 cm-1) and the paper's statement that G broadening starts at the D/G maximum. The I_D/I_G value itself (1.19) cannot tell the two branches apart; I_D/I_G = 1.19 at 532 nm is near the peak region.
The L_D relation was applied outside its stated low-defect regime for dose 3 (L_D ≈ 11 nm vs the paper's L_D >= 10 nm); the result is only marginally inside the validity range.

The absolute defect density depends on the constant C = (1.8 ± 0.5)e-9 nm^2 (±28%) and on the convention n_D = 1e14/(pi L_D^2); the second is my convention, not checked against the paper's definition. Only ratios between doses are robust.
The calibration constant was checked against the paper's Fig. 4 solid curve by reading the plot, not by reading eq. 3 text; the constant could differ by ~20-30%.
The Lorentzian height ratio and the area ratio differ by 5-25% (dose 3: 1.19 vs 1.26). Literature normally uses one of these; the choice shifts L_D by up to ~5%.
The ratio depends on the excitation energy through lambda^4 (532 nm used). Dose 1-3 defect densities scale with I_D/I_G and would change by ×2.3 to 532 nm if the laser energy were off by ~20%.

Dose 4 2D fit hits its width bound (FWHM 120 cm-1); the 2D/G value there is unreliable, though the ~50x drop is clear. D' at dose 4 is merged into G, so the G position and width at dose 4 are merged-band values.
Si line intensity varies ±20% between steps (focus or alignment), so absolute intensities across doses are not comparable; only within-spectrum ratios are used.

The dose 4 G up-shift (+11 cm-1) is attributed to disorder. p-doping can also shift G up, but doping usually narrows G, and G broadens here (14 → 46 cm-1), so doping is not the leading explanation. No 2D-position shift was used to separate the two (2D at dose 4 is unfit).
Possible alternative for dose 4: contamination, a changed spot, or laser-induced damage that also alters the D/G ratio. The spot identity across steps is not documented.
questions_for_user: What is the 'dose'? Ar+ or other ion dose (ions/cm²), electron dose, plasma or laser dose? Converting the defect density into a per-dose efficiency needs the nominal dose in ions/cm². The stage-1 relation assumes point-defect (ion-type) disorder; other damage types can behave differently.
Was the same spot measured at each dose, and was the laser power (nominal 1 mW) verified at each step? The Si intensity changes by ±20% between spectra, which suggests focus or alignment drift.
Is the dose 4 spectrum from the same spot? The loss of 2D and the G broadening are large enough that a contaminated or amorphised area is possible.
Was the substrate or flake thickness checked at each step (for example by optical contrast)? The monolayer assignment here is inferred from 2D width and 2D/G only.
Do you have a reference spectrum of pristine graphene on the same substrate and at 532 nm? That gives an undamaged G position and width to test the doping and strain alternatives directly.
citations: arXiv:1105.0175 (Cancado et al., Nano Letters 2011, as I recall it; the iopic-bond library holds this preprint with five figures) — Fig. 3 (I_D/I_G vs L_D; stage 1 for L_D > 3 nm, maximum at L_D ~ 3 nm, stage 2 below), Fig. 4 (E_L^4 I_D/I_G vs L_D; low-defect regime L_D >= 10 nm; stage-1 solid curve), Fig. 5(c) (G FWHM ~14 cm-1 constant until the onset of stage 2 at max I_D/I_G).
limits: I used only the four CSVs in the working folder. The skill's scripts, reference notes and material literature note live outside that folder; per the instructions I did not read them. All fitting was my own scipy/lmfit code.

The stage-1 constant (1.8e-9 nm^2) and the stage boundaries are from arXiv:1105.0175 (Fig. 3, 4, 5 as read from the figures and captions); I did not parse eq. 1 or eq. 3 text. Confirm against the published Nano Letters version before quoting numbers.
The defect-density convention n_D = 1e14/(pi L_D^2) is my own; check it against the paper's definition.
The monolayer thresholds (2D FWHM ~32 cm-1 and 2D/G ≈ 3) are standard expectations I did not verify against a source here.
Stage 2 cannot be converted to an L_D or density with the stage-1 relation. The dose 4 L_D of order 1-2 nm is a rough read of the dotted curve in Fig. 4 and is not a fit result.
The data cannot tell the dose type or the absolute number of defects. Only the ratio of D/G and the relative changes across doses are measured.
Raman alone cannot separate sp2 vacancy density from amorphous carbon fraction at dose 4; XPS, TEM or a pristine reference would be needed.
The Si line at 520.9 cm-1 is compared to the nominal 520.7 cm-1 from general knowledge, not from a file in this folder.
